deepDive.title: McKinsey: AI Agents Are Undercutting Banks' Automation Dividends
deepDive.html:
Overview

McKinsey has fired a direct warning at bank executives: the costs of deploying AI agents are quietly consuming the very savings they were supposed to generate. The analysis flags a structural trap many banks are already walking into — incremental agent deployments funded by savings that haven't materialised yet.

The Details

  • McKinsey finds that siloed, department-by-department agentic AI rollouts drive overhead costs that outpace efficiency gains.
  • Legacy core banking integration is the primary cost driver — connecting agents to decades-old systems is orders of magnitude more expensive than connecting them to cloud-native infrastructure.
  • Banks that automated on legacy RPA face disproportionately high upgrade costs when transitioning to agentic architectures.
  • Governance and monitoring infrastructure for autonomous agents adds a cost layer that most business cases never modelled.
  • McKinsey's prescription: only coordinated, enterprise-wide agentic deployments with centralised cost accounting achieve net-positive automation economics.

Why It Matters

This report should be required reading for every bank CFO approving AI agent project proposals. The pattern McKinsey describes — acquiring automation savings with one hand while spending them with the other — is precisely what happens when agent pilots are greenlit silo by silo, without central ROI tracking. Banks with dozens of active pilots and no enterprise cost model are running a risk they haven't yet priced.

The implication for asset managers and insurers is equally pointed: agentic AI is not a drop-in upgrade to existing automation stacks. Firms that model ROI without accounting for agent governance, inference costs, and legacy plumbing will consistently overpromise. The winners will design enterprise AI architectures — and full total-cost models — before procurement, not after the pilots have already proliferated.

items.tagline: Real-time guardrails platform that prevents autonomous AI agents from taking harmful or unauthorised actions inside enterprise systems
items.summary: Bay has raised $50 million to address a rapidly emerging risk as banks and enterprises roll out autonomous agents with live access to customer data, trading systems, and internal workflows.
items.analysis: **Filling the enterprise safety gap.** Bay focuses on in-flight agent action controls — not just model-level safety — which is directly relevant to banks deploying agentic workflows with access to accounts, transactions, or regulated data.

items.tagline: Payment infrastructure that gives AI agents their own isolated, controlled spending accounts — Agent Vaults
items.summary: Rain has launched Agent Vaults: dedicated payment accounts for AI agents that isolate agent-initiated spending from business accounts and enforce real-time spending limits and audit trails.
items.analysis: **Solving agent payment governance.** As agentic AI begins executing financial transactions autonomously, Rain's vault model gives banks and fintechs a compliant, auditable framework for agent payments — a governance gap most enterprise AI deployments have yet to address.

items.tagline: Agentic AI platform for tax professionals that automates complex tax research, analysis, and advice workflows
items.summary: Blue J has raised $176 million in a Series E at over $700 million valuation to scale its agentic tax AI — a system built to handle the nuanced, multi-step reasoning that tax and financial advisory work requires.
items.analysis: **High-stakes agentic AI at scale.** Tax and regulatory compliance are among the highest-liability AI use cases; Blue J's $700M+ valuation signals serious institutional confidence that agentic AI can handle complex financial reasoning reliably enough for professional practice.

items.headline: Deutsche Bank and Ant set out roadmap for integrating agentic AI into wholesale banking
items.summary: Deutsche Bank and Ant Group have published a joint roadmap for embedding agentic AI across wholesale banking operations, covering trade finance, treasury, and client services. The collaboration signals growing institutional confidence in autonomous agents for high-value banking workflows.
items.keyPoint: **First-mover benchmark.** Two global financial heavyweights going public with a wholesale agentic AI roadmap sets a competitive precedent — peers without a comparable plan will face pressure to accelerate their own timelines.

items.headline: BPI pilots agentic AI for small business loan approvals
items.summary: Bank of the Philippine Islands is piloting an agentic AI system to automate small business loan approval decisions, reducing manual review time and broadening credit access for underserved SME segments in the Philippines.
items.keyPoint: **Credit automation moves into production.** BPI's pilot is an early real-world test of agentic AI in lending decisions — a space where explainability requirements, bias risk, and regulatory scrutiny will intensify fast as adoption spreads.

items.headline: With IPO looming, Anthropic launches new AI models, workplace tools
items.summary: Anthropic has launched new AI models and enterprise workplace tools ahead of a reported IPO. The release includes updates to Claude-based products aimed at enterprise workflows, as the company accelerates commercialisation of its model stack.
items.keyPoint: **Vendor risk calculus shifts.** An Anthropic IPO changes the procurement calculus for banks using Claude-based tools — expect stricter SLAs, broader enterprise support tiers, and increased competitive pressure on AI vendor pricing.

items.headline: Amazon Replaces Claude Sonnet 4.6 With In-House Model, Cutting Ticket-Processing Costs by 98%
items.summary: Amazon has replaced a third-party Claude model with a proprietary in-house model for internal ticket processing, reporting a 98% reduction in per-ticket AI inference costs. The move highlights the economics of vertically-integrated AI for high-volume repetitive enterprise workflows.
items.keyPoint: **Build vs buy — with numbers.** Amazon's 98% cost reduction after moving to an in-house model is a data point every bank CTO will cite when making the case for internal model development at scale.

items.headline: BioCatch Launches AI Detection Tool to Identify Automated Agents in Online Banking
items.summary: BioCatch has launched a behavioural AI tool that distinguishes between human users and AI agents during online banking sessions — helping banks detect unauthorised automation, bot-driven fraud, and account takeover at login and transaction stages.
items.keyPoint: **Detecting the agent in the room.** As AI agents proliferate in both legitimate use and fraud, BioCatch's ability to fingerprint agent behaviour in real time gives banks a critical fraud-detection layer that complements existing identity and access controls.

items.headline: Northern Trust leans on Microsoft FDEs to boost agentic buildout
items.summary: Northern Trust is embedding Microsoft field deployment engineers directly into its AI buildout, using hands-on vendor expertise to accelerate agentic AI deployment across custody, fund administration, and wealth management operations.
items.keyPoint: **The co-deployment model is emerging.** Northern Trust's approach — cloud vendor engineers working inside the bank — is becoming a blueprint for large financial institutions without sufficient internal AI headcount to execute ambitious agentic programmes alone.
